paper.title_en: Conceptual design of a heavy-water-moderated "$^{3}$He+CF$_4$" scintillation neutron detector for nuclear astrophysics measurement
paper.abstract_en: Accurate measurement of critical data for astrophysical modeling, such as ($\alpha $, n) and ($\gamma $, n) cross-sections and $\beta $-delayed neutron emission probabilities, depends heavily on overcoming the low and energy/emission-angle-dependent efficiency of current polyethylene-moderated $^3$He neutron detectors. We proposed a novel detector that replaces polyethylene with a large spherical heavy-water-moderator and substitutes $^3$He tubes with a layer of "$^3$He + CF$_4$" scintillation gas coupled to photomultipliers for thermal neutron detection. Simulations performed with MCNPX under varied moderator configurations show that a design employing 7.0 cm boron-11, 0.9 cm beryllium, and 50.0 cm heavy water achieves a neutron capture efficiency of 85.1%, with less sensitivity to neutron energy and emission angle. The newly designed neutron detector demonstrates its potential to replace the conventional polyethylene moderated $^{3}$He neutron detector and may enable the researchers to make accurate measurements of ($\alpha $, n), ($\gamma $, n) cross-sections and $\beta $-delayed neutron emission probabilities.
